A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe Self-Speculative Masked Diffusions. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. The experimental details in v1 Appendix E are retained as v2 Appendix G.

before.justification: v1 reports original training, generation, and ablation results on Text8, OpenWebText, and UniRef50, including Table 1 and Figures 2–4, 6, and 7.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results on all three datasets, including the architectural ablations and appendix training curves and generated samples.

M1.justification: The hybrid non-causal/causal architecture, joint training objective, and sampling Algorithms 2–3 are retained. Added training/inference explanations and explicit boundary and rounding conventions clarify the specification without establishing a changed underlying implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions train or evaluate on Text8, OpenWebText, and UniRef50 with the same generation tasks. The added appendix analyses introduce no dataset, population, or test scenario.

E2.justification: The corresponding masked-diffusion baselines remain throughout, and OpenWebText retains Self-Distillation Through Time (SDTT). The newly cited Peng et al. (2025) method is discussed but not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Training budgets, sample sizes, metrics, NFE accounting, and benchmark evaluation procedures remain unchanged in Section 5 and the experimental-details appendix. The one-verification-step settings highlighted in v2 Table 2 already appear in v1's Text8 sampling-settings table.

E4.justification: New Appendix E adds an analytical breakdown of computational overhead for the OpenWebText architecture. Appendix F revisits existing architectural ablations and sampling-parameter results; it does not establish additional robustness tests or newly run ablations.

E5.justification: Figure 4 retains mean protein pLDDT over 512 samples with standard-error shading. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Appendix E newly reports analytical estimates of 3.7e11 FLOPs for the vanilla transformer and 3.6e9 additional FLOPs, stated as 0.98% overhead. Table 1 and the existing result curves and generated examples are unchanged. New Table 2 tabulates Text8 points from the existing tradeoff curve, rather than demonstrating improved performance.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly states p(i = D) = 0, specifies flooring in the cosine-window definition, and adds an architecture-specific FLOP derivation. Lemma C.1 receives a shorter direct proof while the principal likelihood and rejection-count results remain unchanged. Equation 1's complementary alpha convention preserves the underlying diffusion process.

C1.justification: The central approximately twofold NFE-reduction claim is retained. The introduction replaces the assertion of a 'strict improvement' over the draft distribution with a target that 'learns to improve,' and the discussion adds the claim of negligible computational overhead quantified as 0.98%.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly acknowledges that methods selecting the generation ordering can attain higher pLDDT, delimiting this paper's uniformly random ordering comparison. Appendix F adds practical tuning guidance and an explicitly speculative extension of the causal-layer tradeoff beyond the tested configurations.

D1.justification: Appendix E specifies embedding reuse, projection of concatenated hidden states and token embeddings from 3C to C, and explicit OpenWebText architecture dimensions. Existing training budgets, hardware, code references, and sampling settings remain in the relocated experimental-details appendix.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hoffmann et al. (2022) as the source of its FLOP-accounting framework and Peng et al. (2025) to contextualize protein generation with optimized orderings. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized revisions clarify training versus inference and the likelihood recursion, condense Lemma C.1's proof, and correct wording. Two appendix sections are inserted, with experimental details relabeled E to G. Publication-header and author-information edits accompany these changes; the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the small Text8 hyperparameter-results table and expands Figure 1's caption to explain its symbols. Existing figures retain their graphical content, while figure/table placement and surrounding pagination change. The former sampling-settings tables are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 provides clearer explanations of information flow and likelihood computation, more explicit implementation details, and useful tuning guidance. It also moderates the strict-improvement assertion and better qualifies the protein comparison. The empirical evidence is retained without changed performance results. The added FLOP estimate is analytical rather than measured runtime evidence, so the overall gain is chiefly clarity and precision.
